purpose: Original sprites for random-map portal networks (docs/portal-networks.md): a two-way Wayring, a one-way Waygate entrance and a Wayfall exit, told apart by shape, with their magic on a separate layer the overworld tints per network.

images.prompt:
A single adventure-map sprite for an original fantasy strategy game: a "Wayring", a two-way travel portal. A tall upright ring of fitted grey granite blocks, perfectly round like a standing stone wheel, set on a low round stepped stone plinth with two shallow steps at the front. Carved runes run around the ring's face. The whole inside of the ring is filled with a flat disc of glowing magical energy turning in a slow even spiral, the same seen from either side, and a soft glow spills onto the plinth.

The magical energy and every bit of its glow are one single vivid pure magenta colour (hue exactly #FF00FF), from deep saturated magenta at the edges to pale bright magenta at the centre. Nothing else in the image is magenta, pink, red or purple: the stonework is cool neutral grey with a little green moss.

Match the style of the reference images exactly: painterly hand-painted fantasy game sprite, rich colours, soft warm key light from the upper left, crisp dark outlines softened by painting, small soft contact shadow. Same elevated three-quarter isometric camera angle as the references, object centered, filling about 60% of the frame with transparent margin around it.

One object only, no people, no creatures, no ground tile beyond the object's own stone base, no scenery, no text, no letters, no frame. Plain transparent background.

Two small carved stone posts flank the bottom step. Inside the arch a deep vortex funnels inward and away: glowing streaks spiral tightly into a black centre, as if the doorway swallows whatever walks in. A thin glowing rim lines the inner edge of the arch.

key_colour: Each painting keeps its magic in pure magenta (#FF00FF) and nothing else in that hue.
packing: tools/pack_portal_network_sprites.py: the magenta-keyed energy moves to a white glow layer (brightness = mean RGB x 1.35) and leaves the stone base; both layers get the same mechanical alpha trim (alpha above 60 for the crop box) and aspect-preserving resize to 300px on the shared 512px transparent canvas, centered and bottom-aligned at y=390; no repainting.
